title: Evaluating the Structural Basis for Polar Altermagnet Candidate Ca$_{3}$(Ru,Ti)$_{2}$O$_{7}$
authors: Akash Saha, Yihuang Xiong, Vladimir A. Stoica, Subin Mali, Aaron Pearre, Saugata Sarker, Huaiyu Wang, Yufei Zhao, Evguenia Karapetrova, Yu Wang, Jadupati Nag, Zachary W. Hazenstab, Seng Huat Lee, Long-Qing Chen, Geoffroy Hautier, Binghai Yan, Zhiqiang Mao, Venkatraman Gopalan
abstract: The interplay between polar and altermagnetic orders remains largely unexplored in the broader landscape of correlated electron systems. Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ has been proposed by density functional theory (DFT) as a polar altermagnet, reliant on the transformation of experimentally reported $Bb2_{1}m$ phase to a lower symmetry $Pn2_{1}a$ structure. Here, we perform a targeted search for the $Pn2_{1}a$ phase using synchrotron X-ray diffraction on single crystals of Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ and Ca$_{3}$(Ru$_{0.99}$Ti$_{0.01}$)$_{2}$O$_{7}$. No diffraction signature of the $Pn2_{1}a$ structure is detected down to 20 K within experimental limits of $\sim$60-200 fm atomic displacements, significantly smaller than the DFT prediction of $\sim$1 pm. Combined with recent nonlinear transport measurements, our structural study suggests Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ as a unique system where strong electron correlations drive an electronic phase transition without any measurable lattice symmetry change. With Ti substitution exceeding $\sim$3%, a chemically tunable altermagnetic phase with $Bb2_{1}m$ structure emerges. The study highlights the importance of sub-picometer metrology towards de-convolving structural versus electronic origins of altermagnets.
summary: The research investigates the structural basis for altermagnetism in $	ext{Ca}_3(	ext{Ru},	ext{Ti})_2	ext{O}_7$. Despite theoretical predictions of a symmetry-lowering phase transition ($Pn21a$), detailed X-ray diffraction experiments found no evidence of this lattice distortion. The authors conclude that the observed electronic symmetry breaking is likely decoupled from measurable structural changes, suggesting an electronically driven mechanism for altermagnetism.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the predicted structural phase transition from a polar altermagnet candidate ($	ext{Ca}_3	ext{Ru}_2	ext{O}_7$) is structurally mandated or purely electronic in origin.
main_result: Experimental X-ray diffraction measurements failed to detect the symmetry-lowering $Pn2_1a$ phase, placing tight upper bounds on structural distortions. Instead, evidence suggests that the observed symmetry breaking is primarily electronic, leading to a chemically tunable G-type altermagnetic (G-ALM) state within the higher symmetry $Bb2_1m$ structure.
method: The work combines synchrotron X-ray diffraction measurements with advanced DFT+U calculations incorporating spin-orbit coupling and Hubbard U parameters.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Ca}_3(	ext{Ru},	ext{Ti})_2	ext{O}_7$, a correlated electron oxide exhibiting complex magnetic ordering (AFM, G-ALM) and potential structural transitions between $Bb2_1m$ and $Pn2_1a$.
key_observables: Diffraction peak intensities ($I_{HKL}$), structural distortion amplitude ($\lambda$), electronic band gap opening, and magnetic transition temperatures ($T_N, T_S$).
important_parameters: The critical comparison is between the DFT-predicted large structural displacement ($\sim 1 	ext{ pm}$) versus the experimentally constrained upper bound on distortion ($\lambda \lesssim 0.08$ to $0.22$), and the role of Ti doping ($x$) as a tuning parameter.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that experimental background noise provides reliable, quantitative upper bounds on structural distortions, and that DFT+U calculations accurately capture the electronic ground state evolution with varying correlation strength (Hubbard U).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between predicted $Bb21m$ and $Pn21a$ structures, show the absence of expected $Pn21a$ diffraction peaks at low temperatures, and map out phase diagrams showing electronic/magnetic transitions as a function of Ti doping or Hubbard U.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical prediction of a structural transition ($Bb21m 	o Pn21a$), then using high-sensitivity X-ray diffraction to experimentally constrain this distortion, and finally reconciling the negative structural findings with positive electronic measurements (nonlinear transport) by proposing an electronically driven symmetry breaking mechanism.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant because it addresses the fundamental question of whether magnetic/electronic phase transitions in correlated oxides are accompanied by measurable lattice distortions or if they can be purely electronic, a key concept in modern condensed matter theory.
